Brande & C. -- Mor`ga*nat"ic*al*ly, adv.

MANRED: Homage or service rendered to a superior, as to a lord; vassalage. [Obs. or Scots Law] Jamieson.

MANDATORY: Containing a command; preceptive; directory. Same as Mandatary.
MESODERMAL: Pertaining to, or derived from, the mesoderm; as, mesodermal tissues.
MAIN YARD: The yard on which the mainsail is extended, supported by the mainmast.
MANUS: The distal segment of the fore limb, including the carpus and fore foot or hand.
METABOLE: A change or mutation; a change of disease, symptoms, or treatment.

MARGRAVE: 1. Originally, a lord or keeper of the borders or marches in Germany. 2. The English equivalent of the German title of nobility, markgraf; a marquis.
MAKE-BELIEVE: A feigning to believe, as in the play of children; a mere pretense; a fiction; an invention. "Childlike make-believe." Tylor. To forswear self-delusion and make-believe. M. Arnold. Feigned; insincere. "Make-believe reverence." G. Eliot.

MISSA: The service or sacrifice of the Mass.
MACRODIAGONAL: The longer of two diagonals, as of a rhombic prism. See Crystallization.

MAMELUCO: A child born of a white father and Indian mother. [S. Amer.]
MISSAY: 1. To say wrongly. 2. To speak evil of; to slander. [Obs.] To speak ill. [Obs.] Spenser.

MYRMIDONIAN: Consisting of, or like, myrmidons. Pope.

MICRONOMETER: An instrument for noting minute portions of time.
MANTRAP: 1. A trap for catching trespassers. [Eng.] 2. A dangerous place, as an open hatch, into which one may fall.

MIMETIC: 1. Apt to imitate; given to mimicry; imitative. 2. (Biol.) Characterized by mimicry; -- applied to animals and plants; as, mimetic species; mimetic organisms. See Mimicry.

MONKEYTAIL: A short, round iron bar or lever used in naval gunnery. Totten.
MAISTRIE: Mastery; superiority; art. See Mastery. [Obs.] Chaucer.

MANHOOD: 1. The state of being man as a human being, or man as distinguished from a child or a woman. 2. Manly quality; courage; bravery; resolution. I am ashamed That thou hast power to shake my manhood thus. Shak.
MAXILLAR: 1. (Anat.) Pertaining to either the upper or the lower jaw, but now usually applied to the upper jaw only. -- n. The principal maxillary bone; the maxilla. 2. (Zoöl.) Of or pertaining to a maxilla.

METAPHYSICALLY: In the manner of metaphysical science, or of a metaphysician. South.
MAGNILOQUENT: Speaking pompously; using swelling discourse; bombastic; tumid in style; grandiloquent. -- Mag*nil"o*quent*ly, adv.

MICRONESIAN: Of or pertaining to Micronesia, a collective designation of the islands in the western part of the Pacific Ocean, embracing the Marshall and Gilbert groups, the Ladrones, the Carolines, etc.

METEOROSCOPE: (a) An astrolabe; a planisphere. [Obs.] (b) An instrument for measuring the position, length, and direction, of the apparent path of a shooting star.

METHODOLOGY: The science of method or arrangement; a treatise on method. Coleridge.
MIDFEATHER: 1. (Steam Boilers) A vertical water space in a fire box or combustion chamber. 2. (Mining) A support for the center of a tunnel.

MEATUS: A natural passage or canal; as, the external auditory meatus. See Illust. of Ear.
METAMERE: One of successive or homodynamous parts in animals and plants; one of a series of similar parts that follow one another in a vertebrate or articulate animal, as in an earthworm; a segment; a somite. See Illust. of Loeven's larva.

MONOSTROPHIC: Having one strophe only; not varied in measure; written in unvaried measure. Milton.
MICROBE: A microscopic organism; -- particularly applied to bacteria and especially to pathogenic forms; as, the microbe of fowl cholera.
MAMMONITE: One devoted to the acquisition of wealth or the service of Mammon. C. Kingsley.

MOROS: The Mohammedan tribes of the southern Philippine Islands, said to have formerly migrated from Borneo. Some of them are warlike and addicted to piracy.
MANLINESS: The quality or state of being manly.
MONOECIAN: 1. (Bot.) Of or pertaining to the Monoecia; monoecious. -- n. One of the Monoecia. 2. (Zoöl.) A monoecious animal, as certain mollusks.

MORPHOLOGIC: Of, pertaining to, or according to, the principles of morphology. -- Mor`pho*log"ic*al*ly, adv.
MARIET: A kind of bellflower, Companula Trachelium, once called Viola Mariana; but it is not a violet.

MEDIATION: 1. The act of mediating; action or relation of anything interposed; action as a necessary condition, means, or instrument; interposition; intervention. MANO: The muller, or crushing and grinding stone, used in grinding corn on a metate. [Mexico & Local U. S.]
MALINGERY: The spirit or practices of a malingerer; malingering.

MARAVEDI: A small copper coin of Spain, equal to three mils American money, less than a farthing sterling. Also, an ancient Spanish gold coin.
MYOPSIS: The appearance of muscæ volitantes. See Muscæ volitantes, under Musca.

MACROSPORE: One of the specially large spores of certain flowerless plants, as Selaginella, etc.

MALFEASANCE: The doing of an act which a person ought not to do; evil conduct; an illegal deed. [Written also malefeasance.]

METEOROLITE: A meteoric stone; an aërolite; a meteorite.

MUCRONULATE: Having, or tipped with, a small point or points.

MAMMOSE: Having the form of the breast; breast-shaped.
MORDICATION: The act of biting or corroding; corrosion. [R.] Bacon.

MANDUCATION: The act of chewing. [R.] Jer. Taylor.
